en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
Discourse on the Cause of Karma:
Is it the case that an Arahant falls away from Arahantship because of karma as a cause? Yes.
Is it because of karma that a stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so …pe… Is it because of karma that an arahant falls away from arahantship?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is it because of karma that a once-returner … [and so on] … a non-returner falls away from the fruit of non-returning?”
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it because of kamma that a stream-enterer does not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is it because of karma that an Arahant does not fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so …pe… is it because of karma that a Sakadāgāmī …pe…?
Is it not the case that a non-returner does not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. Is it not the case that an arahant, by reason of his karma, does not fall away from arahantship?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Is it the case that, by reason of karma, an Arahant falls away from Arahantship? Yes.
Is it because of the action of taking life?
One should not say so …pe… Is it because of the action of taking what is not given? …pe…
Because of the karma of sexual misconduct,
because of the karma of false speech,
because of the karma of divisive speech...
Because of the kamma of harsh speech … because of the kamma of idle chatter … because of the kamma of matricide …
Because of the karma of killing one’s father … because of the karma of killing an arahant … because of the karma of shedding blood … [and so forth] …
Is it for the sake of the formal act of causing a schism in the Saṅgha?
One should not say so … [as before] … For the sake of what kind of action?
Indeed, he slanders the Arahants.
Is it because of that act of slandering the Arahants that an Arahant falls away from Arahantship?
Yes, [you say].
"Is it the case that all who misrepresent Arahants have realized Arahantship?
"One should not say so... [etc.
...The Discussion on the Cause of Karma is finished.
The Eighth Chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
The six destinies, the intermediate state, the five strands of sensual pleasure, the realm of sense-desire, the five bases that are sensual pleasures, and those possessing form.
Phenomena are the form element; non-material phenomena are the formless element; the sixfold base constitutes the personal existence within the form element;
there is form within the formless states; form is karma; form is life; and that which is caused by karma may decline.
